subject.title: fix(line): bound inbound media download body reads

question: Should inbound LINE media that continues transferring past 120 seconds fail through the media-unavailable path, while retaining the existing 15-second readiness-poll limit?
rationale: The code structure avoids starving late-ready media and has strong controlled proof, but the precise fail-closed duration deliberately changes delivery behavior for slow valid attachments and cannot be selected from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Confirm the 120-second body cap
options.body: Accept bounded failure for exceptionally slow valid transfers, retain separate 15-second readiness and 120-second body budgets, and merge after a current-main refresh.

options.title: Choose a different owner policy
options.body: Pause this PR until the LINE owner selects a different bounded duration or delivery policy and the focused tests and proof are updated to match.

recommendation.title: Confirm the 120-second body cap
recommendation.body: Accept bounded failure for exceptionally slow valid transfers, retain separate 15-second readiness and 120-second body budgets, and merge after a current-main refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current LINE-specific readiness and stream-handling contract that this PR extends.
